To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Aspirin‐triggered 15‐(R)‐hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (ATL) is a biomarker of lung cyclooxygenase 2 (COX‐2) in vivo but not of plasma COX‐2.

(a) aspirin‐trigger lipoxin (ASITL) levels are increased in the lungs of mice treated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and aspirin, but not in the plasma of LPS‐ and aspirin‐treated mice; (b) the increase in ASITL in the lungs is associated with an increase in COX‐2 levels in the lungs of these mice; and (c) the increase in COX2 in the lungs
Aspirin‐triggered 15‐EPI‐LXA4 (ATL) is detectable in the lungs of lipopolysaccharide‐treated C57Bl6 mice but not in their plasma, and that ATL levels are not a biomarker for vascular COX‐1 or COX‐2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs for treating cardiovascular disease.
the role of COX-2 in the pathogenesis of vascular disease, and with the development of a biomarker for COX-2.
the development and application of novel analytical techniques to the study of the human metabolome and how it is affected by disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plasma ATL is not an accurate biomarker of CO2 in the lungs or the vascular system.
aspirin‐triggering 15‐epilipoxin A‐4 is not a useful marker of COX‐1 or COX‐2 activity in the circulation.
aspirin triggers 15‐epilpoxin A4 production in lung but not plasma of LPS‐induced mice, which is a biomarker of pulmonary COX‐2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aspirin triggers 15‐epoxy‐lipoxin‐A4 in the lungs of mice treated with endotoxin, but that this does not happen in the plasma.
aspirin triggers 15‐epoxyeicosatrienoic acid and 15‐epiloxin A4 production in tissues, but not plasma, in mice.
aspirin‐trigged lipoxin A4 (15‐epi) is not a biomaker for COX‐2 activity in the circulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plasma levels of aspirin-triggered lipoxin A4 are not a biomarker for COX-2 in the circulation.
aspirin‐triggering lipoxins are formed in the lung and not the circulation.
plasma levels of ATL cannot be used as a marker of COX‐1 or COX‐2 activity in the vasculature.
